[SCENE GEOMETRY & ARCHITECTURE]
A documentary medium-format aerial photograph of the National Mall and the Washington Monument in Washington, D.C., captured on a Mamiya 7 with a 45mm wide-angle lens on Kodak Ektar 100 fine-grain film at f/8, corner-to-corner tack sharpness, corrected for perspective tilt with razor-sharp vertical planar rectification. In the center, the monumental 169-meter-tall Washington Monument obelisk rises plumb to the sky from its circular stone plaza, displaying the distinct subtle horizontal color shift at the 46-meter line between the lower historic Cockeysville marble courses and the upper marble shaft, showing realistic rain-wash channels and soft atmospheric stone patina. To the right and northeast, the monumental Beaux-Arts Indiana limestone facades of the Federal Triangle complex extend along Constitution Avenue with their grand Doric colonnades, rusticated plinths, and terracotta-red barrel-tiled hipped roofs, contrasted by the dark bronze filigree corona tiers of the National Museum of African American History and Culture. In the distance to the north, the tree-fringed green lawn of the Ellipse leads toward the White House grounds. The wide-angle perspective reveals lush, mature American elm allees, grand sycamores, and textured manicured lawns laced with curving gravel and asphalt pedestrian paths. Hard, clear, early-morning raking sunlight casts a long, sharp, dark directional shadow of the obelisk extending westward across the bright green expanse.
